title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) executed under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded under the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Confirmatory execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for a confirmatory safety verdict; the frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validator traces required to compute that aggregation were recorded during execution and enable deterministic independent recomputation. We present the preregistered primary result, clarify execution semantics, expand interpretation of discordant-pair structure and observed failure modes, and state limitations and reproducibility guidance without altering the preregistered scientific record.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are fed back to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior controlled and benchmark studies in code, Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC), and domain-specific languages report that adding deterministic verifiers can increase verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes (for example, verifier-exploitation) and imposing interaction costs [1]–[4]. Field and survey work about LLMs in NetOps/AIOps indicates that read-oriented assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed-loop autonomous changes and motivates conservative verification and orchestration [5].

This study addresses a specific empirical gap: controlled paired evidence on whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow improves end-to-end verifier+simulator-validated correctness on vendor-CLI templates when repairs must address preregistered deterministic faults. We used deterministic controlled faults to guarantee intervention activation and an explicit shared-candidate paired design so both arms received the exact same initial faulty candidate. Our primary research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics?
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair and verifier-mediated refinement have been studied across multiple application domains. Empirical pipeline evaluations in code and IaC show that deterministic verifiers interposed between generation and acceptance raise verifier pass rates and that supplying verifier diagnostics to repair models increases the probability that corrected artifacts satisfy the verifier on recheck [doi:10.2139/ssrn.6754899; https://openalex.org/W7171267824]. Complementary analyses document caveats: optimization toward a single verifier proxy can lead to verifier-exploitation (improved proxy metrics with degraded target properties) [doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10187492/v1], and verifier-mediated workflows incur nontrivial interaction and compute overheads (the “verifier tax”) that depend on horizon and design [http://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19328]. Surveys and field case studies of LLM use in NetOps emphasize that LLMs are strongest for read-oriented and diagnostic assistance, while closed-loop autonomous configuration changes require careful validation and governance to avoid unsafe outcomes [https://openalex.org/W7161165783].

The supplied literature motivates our controlled-challenge choice: (1) use deterministic verifiers and a simulator-backed acceptance predicate to make the primary outcome operationally interpretable within the experiment, (2) ensure repair-trigger activation by injecting deterministic faults, and (3) use shared-candidate paired semantics so condition differences isolate diagnostic exposure rather than first-pass sampling differences. The present study complements prior IaC and code demonstrations by focusing on vendor-CLI templates and by preregistering a harmful-change labeling mapping to support safety-oriented secondary aggregations.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a per-pair binary success required both the deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance agreement.

Adapter, pairing, and generation semantics. Confirmatory execution used the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics. Under that contract, for each task index the deterministic controlled-fault generator produced exactly one shared faulty candidate which was reused unchanged across both experimental conditions; exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was performed and reused by both arms. Baseline denotes blind repair (repair without exposure of verifier diagnostics) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed to the repair model. Because the same sampled initial candidate and matched repair budget were used in both arms, observed differences isolate the effect of exposing diagnostics under the adapter semantics.

Model sampling and runtime parameters. Confirmatory execution declared model gpt-5-mini. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was reused under the adapter contract; the design does not measure effects of independent first-pass sampling across conditions.

Controlled-challenge fault bank and scoring rule. We preregistered a 40-index controlled-fault bank produced by a deterministic_netops_fault_injector and a primary success predicate requiring agreement of the deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator-based compliance check. A frozen harmful-change labeling mapping defined operational harmful codes (for example PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE and UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE) and was recorded before execution. All per-episode validator traces and transformation mappings needed to compute preregistered secondary safety aggregations were recorded during execution.

Statistical analysis plan. The prespecified primary test was a two-sided exact paired binary test (exact McNemar or equivalent). We report discordant-pair counts (n10, n01), the absolute paired risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (resamples = 10000, seed = 1729), and the two-sided exact p-value. Missingness followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule (exclude a pair only if both executions are unscorable); sensitivity options treating missing episodes as failures were preregistered.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes yielded 39 complete pairs after one source generation was invalid and excluded under the preregistered rule. Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded per the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule because its source generation was invalid/unscorable; terminal error reasons were logged in the archived execution manifest.

Confirmatory harmful-overrepair statistic: status. The preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation was not computed in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore is not reported here as a confirmatory quantity. The frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validation traces required to compute that preregistered safety aggregation were recorded during execution and enable deterministic independent recomputation; any such counts produced outside the archived confirmatory summary are exploratory.
sections.discussion:
Primary-effect interpretation and discordant-pair structure. The paired result indicates a statistically detectable and operationally meaningful improvement in verifier+simulator-validated success when deterministic verifier diagnostics were exposed to the repair model under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics. The discordant-pair pattern (n10 = 9 guarded-only successes vs n01 = 1 baseline-only success) implies that most of the observed improvement arises from guarded repairs recovering otherwise failing shared candidates rather than guarded introducing novel failures that baseline avoided. Because the shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics guarantee identical initial faulty input to both arms and matched repair budgets, these discordant counts isolate the diagnostic-exposure effect under the adapter contract rather than first-pass sampling or differing repair-call budgets.

Failure-mode diagnostics grounded in validator traces. Per-episode validator_trace records show a small vocabulary of repeating violation codes driving failure cases: PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE, and FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH appear frequently among failing baseline episodes. Representative artifacts illustrate how exposing validator diagnostics enabled targeted edits: for example, task-000003 (difficulty level "hard" in the manifest) contained PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE and UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE in the baseline post-repair trace and was scored fail (score = 0) in baseline, while the guarded repair for the same shared candidate produced a configuration with the violating codes removed and was scored pass. These per-episode traces support a mechanistic interpretation: validator diagnostics frequently identify protected fields or unintended-state edits, and exposing those diagnostics to the repair model yields focused corrective edits that avoid or restore protected fields and required command sequences that blind repair sometimes omitted.

Difficulty stratification and representative-task evidence. The task manifest entries recorded per-task difficulty labels (for example "medium", "hard", "very_hard") and required command sequences. Representative examples in the archived artifacts show guarded repairs recovering some "hard" cases that baseline failed (illustrated by task-000003). We do not present a confirmatory per-difficulty subgroup analysis because that secondary estimand was prespecified but treated as exploratory; with complete_pairs = 39 the study has limited precision for subgroup inference and such stratified estimates should be treated as descriptive.

Statistical uncertainty, power, and preregistered planning. The preregistration planned n = 40 pairs aiming to detect a large absolute paired difference (~30 percentage points) with reasonable power. The observed absolute paired difference (~20.51 percentage points) is smaller than the original planning target but still produced a two-sided exact p = 0.021 and a paired-bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero. Nonetheless, the finite paired sample (39 complete pairs) limits inference granularity: CI width and the small number of discordant pairs constrain precision for secondary or subgroup contrasts and preclude strong claims about per-fault-class heterogeneity.

Operational implications and verifier tax. Guarded repair materially improved the preregistered verifier+simulator pass predicate on this controlled fault bank, but adapter-mediated verification incurs interaction costs: the confirmatory run consumed 118 hosted-model calls under the matched budget. These counts permit exploratory per-avoided-failure cost computations, but broad operational feasibility (cost/latency tradeoffs, orchestration overheads) requires larger-scale deployment studies under realistic task streams.

Safety boundary and unresolved preregistered aggregation. The preregistered confirmatory safety test bounding harmful over-repair was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference. The frozen harmful-change mapping (definition: episodes marked harmful if post-repair validator traces include PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE) and all per-episode validator traces were recorded and enable deterministic independent recomputation of the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic; until that recomputation appears in a confirmatory artifact, any safety claims based on post-hoc aggregation must be treated as exploratory.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared-candidate pairing and an exactly-one initial sampled generation per pair ensure that observed differences reflect exposure to diagnostics under matched generation and repair budgets; however, model sampling nondeterminism remains because the archived temperature field is null/unset and does not imply deterministic sampling. Construct validity: the primary success predicate required agreement between a deterministic vendor-CLI validator and a simulator; both components constrain what “valid” means operationally and depend on verifier coverage and simulator fidelity. External validity: confirmatory execution used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), one adapter family, and a synthetic template-based controlled-fault bank, limiting generalization to other models, adapter designs, vendors, or live operator streams. Conclusion validity: with complete_pairs = 39 the study detects the observed primary contrast but has limited power for many secondary comparisons.

Mitigations and future evaluations. Mitigations to verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies include multi-verifier ensembles, explicit harmful-change constraints enforced at acceptance, calibrated abstention, and uncertainty quantification. Operational validation should prioritize (1) recomputing the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation from the frozen mapping and recorded traces, (2) replication across additional models and diverse vendor templates, and (3) end-to-end cost/latency studies to quantify verifier tax under realistic task arrival processes.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using a hosted validator-feedback repair adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). The finding is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the deterministic verifier and simulator used in execution. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not computed in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validation traces recorded during execution provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction of that preregistered safety statistic. We recommend independent recomputation of the preregistered safety aggregation, multi-model replication, and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter family used for confirmatory execution: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini. Exact initial master prompt archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role and autonomy boundary: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change labeling mapping used to define the planned safety aggregation was frozen before execution; the mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation were recorded during execution. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and transformation mappings needed to reproduce the preregistered secondary aggregations were recorded in the archived evidence bundle. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and counts were recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and the frozen mapping required to compute it were recorded and are available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
